Malicious code in saeka (PyPI)

  • saeka

The request requires use of the checking feature; installation or import alone does not trigger it. Version 15.0 also includes bulk card checking and a Shopify checkout flow. entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-h8m9-jgf8-vwvp: Prowler: SAML Domain Claiming Enables Cross-Tenant Account Takeover

Prowler: SAML Domain Claiming Enables Cross-Tenant Account Takeover

Aliases: CVE-2026-100169, CVE-2026-59151, PYSEC-2026-3725

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • prowler-cloud — fixed in 5.30.3

## SAML Tenant Binding Enables Cross-Tenant Account Takeover ### Summary Prowler's SAML authentication flow trusted the email domain asserted in a SAMLResponse when deciding which tenant should receive the final token. A malicious tenant with its own SAML configuration and a self-controlled IdP could complete a valid SAML flow for its own configured domain, while asserting an email address from another configured domain. In the vulnerable flow, the ACS finish logic later derived the tenant from the asserted email domain instead of binding token issuance to the tenant associated with the validated SAML configuration. This could cause a token to be issued for the wrong tenant. The attacker does not generally need to claim the victim's email domain. If the victim tenant already has SAML c…

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-3725: Prowler is a cloud security platform. Prior to 5.30.3, Prowler's SAML authentication flow trusted the email domain asser
entry.content:
Aliases: CVE-2026-100169, CVE-2026-59151, GHSA-h8m9-jgf8-vwvp

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • prowler-cloud — fixed in 5.30.3

Prowler is a cloud security platform. Prior to 5.30.3, Prowler's SAML authentication flow trusted the email domain asserted in a SAMLResponse when deciding which tenant should receive the final token, and the ACS finish logic in api/src/backend/api/v1/views.py recalculated the tenant from user.email instead of binding token issuance to the validated SAML configuration. An authenticated attacker with a controlled SAML IdP could complete a valid SAML flow for an attacker-controlled domain while asserting an email address from another configured domain, causing a SAMLToken and tenant-scoped JWT to be issued for the wrong tenant and enabling cross-tenant account takeover. This issue is fixed in version 5.30.3.

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-xpf3-p7gm-7756: BBOT's Symlink guard bypass in unarchive module allows planting symlinks during extraction
entry.content:
BBOT's Symlink guard bypass in unarchive module allows planting symlinks during extraction

Aliases: CVE-2026-14966, PYSEC-2026-3719

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • bbot — fixed in 3.0.0

BBOT's `unarchive` module rejects archives containing symlink entries before extraction, but for zip and 7z archives it failed to detect symlinks whose listing carries a DOS-attribute prefix before the unix mode, as produced by legacy versions of p7zip. Such an archive, downloaded and extracted during a scan (for example via `filedownload`), bypassed the guard and caused an attacker-controlled symlink to be written into the extraction directory. The effect is limited to planting the symlink (its target is not written through), and only hosts using such a legacy p7zip build are affected; current mainline 7-Zip is not.

References:

  • https://github.com/blacklanternsecurity/bbot/security/advisories/GHSA-xpf3-p7gm-7756

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-856c-92hv-3vxx: Apprise forwards configured auth headers across cross-origin HTTP redirects
entry.content:
Apprise forwards configured auth headers across cross-origin HTTP redirects

Aliases: CVE-2026-59180

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • apprise — fixed in 1.11.0

# Summary Apprise's HTTP-based notification plugins and its HTTP attachment / config loaders (`apprise/attachment/http.py`, `apprise/config/http.py`) follow HTTP 3xx redirects by default and **re-send the user-configured auth headers and query parameters on the redirected request**. If an operator-configured destination is later compromised (service takeover, malicious update), or an attacker holds a MITM position on an unprotected network path, that destination can return a `302 Location:` to an arbitrary host and Apprise forwards the user's secret (`X-Gotify-Key`, `Authorization`, bearer tokens in query, custom `+Header=` values) to that cross-origin host. The attacker does **not** need to control the original Apprise URL — only the response from a destination the operator already trust…

## Unauthenticated Command Execution via HTTP MCP `execute_module` ### Summary The HTTP MCP endpoint (`POST /mcp`) in flyto-core accepts unauthenticated JSON-RPC `tools/call` requests and dispatches them to arbitrary registered modules, including `sandbox.execute_shell`, which passes attacker-controlled input directly to `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell`. entry.content:
Malicious code in pyyi (PyPI)

Affected:

  • pyyi

The verified PyPI wheel declares a console command named python2 (pyyi.cli:main). For commands other than the local REPL, help, version, unlock, or uninstall paths, it obtains configuration and calls run_payload(). Registration sends the hostname and OS to a configured space-z.ai server and stores the returned apiKey in ~/.python2/config.json. The REPL presents a normal Python banner but silently sends eligible single-token inputs to /api/cli/unlock as the password field, subject to filtering and attempt limits. run_payload() fetches code from /api/cli/payload, base64-decodes and gzip-decompresses it, then executes it in memory using exec(compile(src, '<adv>', 'exec'), g) at pyyi/cli.py:640 and calls its main function. Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • praisonaiagents — fixed in 4.5.128

## Summary The approval system in PraisonAI Agents caches tool approval decisions by tool name only, not by invocation arguments. Once a user approves `execute_command` for any command (e.g., `ls -la`), all subsequent `execute_command` calls in that execution context bypass the approval prompt entirely. Combined with `os.environ.copy()` passing all process environment variables to subprocesses, this allows an LLM agent (potentially via prompt injection) to silently exfiltrate API keys and credentials without further user consent. ## Details The `require_approval` decorator in `src/praisonai-agents/praisonaiagents/approval/__init__.py:176-178` checks approval status by tool name only: ```python @wraps(func) def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): if is_already_approved(tool_name): # line 17…

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2021-108: An issue was discovered in urllib3 before 1.26.5. When provided with a URL containing many @ characters in the authority
entry.content:
Aliases: CVE-2021-33503, GHSA-q2q7-5pp4-w6pg

Affected:

  • urllib3 — fixed in 2d4a3fee6de2fa45eb82169361918f759269b4ec, 1.26.5

An issue was discovered in urllib3 before 1.26.5. When provided with a URL containing many @ characters in the authority component, the authority regular expression exhibits catastrophic backtracking, causing a denial of service if a URL were passed as a parameter or redirected to via an HTTP redirect.
